clue.text: Spillage container attached to tits — not good, economy-wise, in the long run?

definitions.text: not good, economy-wise, in the long run

indicators.note: one piece is joined straight onto the other, end to end

parts.note: a boom is the floating barrier laid round an oil spill to hold it in
slang for breasts, so a bust

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a drip catcher fixed to a bosom, swerving into a sober point about economics.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOM-BUST describes an economy lurching between expansion and collapse; over time the cycle does more harm than steady growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom-and-bust cycle is the classic example of unsound management that looks fine in the short term.

clue.text: Not much of a Cliff fan? There's a sizeable number inside!

indicators.note: the numeral is placed within the word for an enthusiast

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A lukewarm Cliff Richard admirer, with a crowd hidden somewhere within.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff seems to be the singer Cliff Richard; it is a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep bank or headland, a modest sort of precipice.

clue.text: Abroad with Nick — it didn't reach our screens

parts.note: out and about, away from home
to nick is British slang for to steal, to take

explanation.surface: A TV item about travelling overseas with someone called Nick that was never broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An out-take is footage cut during editing and so never shown to viewers.

clue.text: Failed utterly as a term for how pre-pubescent boys should be tackled?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: made a complete mess of something, in crude British slang

definitions.text: how pre-pubescent boys should be tackled
definitions.meaning: second meaning, a joke: with their balls still up, since young boys' testicles have not yet dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The British slang for botching a job is reread as describing boys whose balls have not yet descended.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballsed up is crude British slang for bungled or completely messed up.

clue.text: Country's brought back broadcasts about "Tony's end"

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the remaining letter
fetched back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: only the last letter of the name

parts.note: Tony Blair, the Prime Minister of the day; his name ends in Y

explanation.surface: A country's media are said to have relayed news about the end of Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East bordering Iraq and Turkey.

clue.text: "Bet Dubya's pissed off with Tony's beginning and end" smear

indicators.note: drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
'off with' cuts the pieces after it out of the letters before

parts.note: taken as written
Dubya is the nickname of George W Bush, written out in full here

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Tony Blair's name, first name only

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Tony Blair's name, first name only

explanation.surface: A mock headline about Bush being drunk and fed up with Tony Blair, framed as a smear.
explanation.walkthrough: Take BET and DUBYA together, knock off the first and last letters of TONY (T and Y), and rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to daub all over, an old-fashioned verb for spreading something messily.

clue.text: Bird's inside leg retroflexed

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of the next two words

parts.note: the bird runs across the break between these two words

explanation.surface: A bird's inner leg is bent backwards, like a heron's knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retroflexed' looks like a reversal signal, but the answer reads forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron, a wading bird of marshes and shores.

clue.text: One repeatedly has way with Woody's ex. — no problem for the red-blooded sort?

definitions.text: no problem for the red-blooded sort?

indicators.note: the ones pair up with the ex, sitting right beside her

parts.note: one given twice over: AN, the indefinite article, then AE, the Scots word for one
Mia Farrow, Woody Allen's former partner

explanation.surface: A man keeps having his way with Woody Allen's former partner, which suits the virile type.
explanation.walkthrough: AE is Scots for one, as in Burns. The red-blooded are the lusty, but taken literally they are people with plenty of red blood cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a shortage of red blood cells, a condition people rich in blood never suffer.

clue.text: How Trigger might be described? Hardly a film star

definitions.meaning: Trigger was Roy Rogers's horse, and a horse wears a bit in its mouth
an actor with only a small part

explanation.walkthrough: Trigger was a cowboy film horse, so the first reading turns on the bit a horse wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit player is an actor given only a minor role, far from stardom.

clue.text: Up to the time when a contemptible type loses head (one left)

indicators.note: the first letter of the insult is dropped

parts.note: the crudest insult for a contemptible person, typical of Private Eye

explanation.surface: A clock-watching phrase followed by someone being beheaded and one person left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Until is the conjunction meaning up to the point in time at which something happens.

clue.text: Brenda rejected by slapper gobbling chap — it causes a delay

indicators.note: sent back, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: Private Eye's long-running nickname for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

indicators.note: the tart swallows the chap, so his name goes inside

parts.note: British slang for a promiscuous woman, a tart
Dan stands for any man here

explanation.surface: The Queen is snubbed by a loose woman busy devouring a man, all of which holds things up.
explanation.walkthrough: In Private Eye the Queen is always Brenda, so Brenda means ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant is a substance that slows down a process such as burning or ripening.

clue.text: Tone upset about Florida's description of politician to whom blame never seems to stick

definitions.text: description of politician to whom blame never seems to stick

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the state abbreviation
knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
FL is the US postal abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A tone of upset over Florida, where the 2000 election left one politician untouched by blame.
explanation.walkthrough: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida. The nickname was first given to Ronald Reagan and later to Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Teflon is a non-stick coating, so a politician on whom scandal never sticks is called Teflon.

clue.text: Iris's snuggled up to Welshman's pole

indicators.note: the two pieces nestle side by side, one straight after the other

parts.note: the yellow flag is a wild iris, so irises are flags
Taff is an old nickname for a Welshman, from the River Taff

explanation.surface: Someone called Iris cuddles up to a Welsh lover from Poland, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality to go with Welshman; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the tall post that a flag is hoisted on.

clue.text: Tiger's tongue in pasta Milanese

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

parts.note: the language runs across the end of pasta and the start of Milanese

explanation.surface: A big cat's tongue turns up in a plate of Milanese pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tigers are the Tamil Tigers of Sri Lanka, and their language is the answer, not a cat's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is the language spoken by the Tamil people, whose separatist guerrillas were called the Tigers.

clue.text: Just the niche for what's pretentious unprocessed crap, right?

definitions.text: Just the niche for what's pretentious

indicators.note: rubbish, done badly, so the letters come out in a botched order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at pretentious art made from raw, unprocessed rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Pseuds Corner is the Private Eye column quoting pretentious writing, so the setter is plugging their own magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine's column collects pompous quotations, a special corner set aside for pretension.

clue.text: Choice writer journo puffed up

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one
a pen is something to write with
an editor, ED, heads the journalists

explanation.surface: A selection of writers and a journalist all grown conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumpen is to make rounder and fuller, so plumpened means swollen out.

clue.text: Jordan appears to be fixing vote: happy Prince goes

indicators.note: rigging a vote means tampering with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for Prince leaves the word happy

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in Jordan rigs a ballot, and a cheerful prince is removed from power.
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan here is Katie Price, the glamour model famous for her surgically enlarged chest, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-heavy describes something with too much weight above, a cheeky description of a big-busted model.

clue.text: Does "love honk' explosively, looking like Punch?

indicators.note: blown apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis scoring, and O looks like zero
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone honks loudly in a show of love, in the manner of a puppet show.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch is the puppet from Punch and Judy, with a huge hooked nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Punch of the British seaside puppet show has a beaky, curved nose.

clue.text: How to get round being wealthy?

definitions.meaning: how you travel around the world
the rich crowd who can afford to fly everywhere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get round' sounds like persuading or becoming fat; it means travelling the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set were wealthy people who flew from one fashionable resort to another.

clue.text: Ready to expose member, end up dithering about Vaz's last sanctimonious U-turn

indicators.note: the mixed letters are put round the rest
wavering this way and that, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of the MP's name is used

parts.note: Keith Vaz, a Labour MP often mocked by Private Eye

indicators.note: the short word for pious is turned to face the other way

parts.note: pious, in its short crossword form

explanation.surface: A sleazy scene in which an MP dithers, and then performs a self-righteous about-face.
explanation.walkthrough: Member is the male member, and the definition describes trousers ready to be opened.
explanation.definitionFit: With the zip undone a man is all set for indecent exposure.

clue.text: Mob size determined by stupid types

indicators.note: the size is worked out afresh, and so the letters are settled into a new order

parts.note: these two words supply exactly the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: How big a crowd gets depends on the idiots in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mob' and 'size' look like the subject; they are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Zombie is a colloquial word for a dull, slow-witted or mindless person.

clue.text: See 14
Hank's out to stifle spirit of ex-President

indicators.note: the jumbled letters smother the drink inside them
the name is put out of order

parts.note: the name is used without its apostrophe-s, which stands for is
a strong drink, here rum

explanation.surface: Someone called Hank sets out to snuff out the ghost of a former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost; it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Kwame Nkrumah led Ghana to independence and served as its first President until 1966.

clue.text: Rank stars penetrated by male solicitors

indicators.note: the male letter goes into the middle of the insignia

parts.note: pips are the small stars on an army officer's shoulder that show rank

explanation.surface: Officers' insignia are pierced by lawyers, or by men, in a typically smutty Private Eye picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitors' suggests lawyers; here it means men who solicit for prostitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimps procure customers for prostitutes, which is soliciting in the legal sense.

clue.text: Has the wherewithal to remove top (black)

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: the phrase is able, written as one string

explanation.surface: Someone with the means to take off a black top.
explanation.walkthrough: Sable is the heraldic word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry and poetry sable is the colour black, from the dark fur.

clue.text: One with invalid charge about US topless knickers

indicators.note: turned around, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accused of a bogus offence involving American knickers with no top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid charge' reads as a false accusation; it means a sick person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick nurse looks after the ill, so a bedridden patient is in her care.

clue.text: Just look at that soldier, one of several sniffing round Brenda

definitions.text: one of several sniffing round Brenda

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier ogling the Queen, one of many admirers round her.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, and her corgis were famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen kept a pack of corgi dogs, which trotted about her feet.

clue.text: He's set to be buggered when the sailors get in

indicators.note: the navy's letters go inside
messed up, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A man fears an assault once the navy arrives, a ribald seaside postcard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just a man's name, Ernst, as in Max Ernst the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst is a German man's first name, so any person called Ernst is a he.

clue.text: Brad snapped "Brenda an anxious type"

parts.note: a brad is a thin nail
bit, as a dog snaps at someone
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, so ER

explanation.surface: An actor called Brad snaps a remark about the Queen being a worrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Brad looks like Brad Pitt; it is a carpentry word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail-biter is a nervous person, from the habit of chewing fingernails under stress.

clue.text: Come see Cyclops in the money

indicators.note: the setter's word goes inside the coin

parts.note: the sen is a small unit of currency in Japan and elsewhere
the setter's pseudonym, so the setter speaking of themself

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and see the setter now rolling in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come' reads as a verb of invitation; it is the vulgar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Come is slang for the fluid ejaculated, the same thing as semen.

clue.text: Wanker's capital changed Kipper

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: tosser is the British slang synonym for this insult

explanation.surface: A rude word for someone gets a new first letter, then a smoked fish appears.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, but here it is one who kips, British slang for sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser sleeps rough or idles, so he is literally someone who kips.

clue.text: Possibly waste of Robin's time, his messing around with Tony's head

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime

indicators.note: fooling about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of the name is taken

parts.note: Tony Blair, the Prime Minister of the day, whose name starts with T

explanation.surface: A complaint that Robin wastes his time while someone messes about with Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin is the bird, not a person; doing bird means serving time in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A robin's droppings are an example of the excrement any small songbird leaves.
